rationale: The student focuses on individual digit size ('nines') instead of looking at the highest place value first. A place-value comparison demonstration comparing numbers with a smaller leading digit but larger subsequent digits (e.g., 2,999 vs 3,001) visually models comparing from the thousands place down and stopping at the first place that differs.
intent: Demonstrate compare on the place-value with values [2999,3001]. Tutor points at: the thousands column

frames.caption: Line up 2,999 and 3,001 by place. Start with the biggest place.
3 thousands is more than 2 thousands, so 3,001 is greater than 2,999. The smaller places cannot catch up, even if they are 9s.

judgement.reasoning: The student believes 3,999 > 4,001 because it has nines. This worked demo explicitly demonstrates comparing 2,999 and 3,001 starting from the thousands place, specifically pointing out that the smaller places cannot catch up even if they are 9s.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this directly addresses the misconception that nines in lower places outweigh a larger digit in the highest place value.
